question: Will the AfD's national polling average in the INSA Sonntagsfrage be at least 30% on November 14, 2026?

calls.reasoning: The five latest INSA polls (3-13 Oct 2026) are 30, 30.5, 30, 30, 30; their median of 30.0 sits exactly on the threshold. The trend has been up about 1pt since late August. The polls that resolve the question are roughly 31 Oct-14 Nov, and a typical 4-week INSA move of about ±1pt makes this close to a coin flip. A slight lean to Yes comes from the upward trend and continuing post-state-election momentum. Against that, the Union just ticked up for the first time in 11 weeks, and record-high readings tend to revert. No prediction market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers.

- Resolves off the wahlrecht.de INSA page: the median of the last 5 AfD values published before 15 Nov 2026 must be >= 30.0. Not off other pollsters or averages.
- Event window: polls published up to 14 Nov 2026, i.e. about the 5 polls from ~31 Oct to 14 Nov. As of 17 Oct, 0% of that window has elapsed.

calls.reasoning: The last 5 INSA AfD readings (Oct 3-13) are 30, 30.5, 30, 30, 30, so the median is exactly 30.0 and would resolve YES today because the bar is inclusive. With 0.5-pt rounding, any true level of 29.75 or more prints 30. The current level is about 30.1, a slight cushion. With a 4-week SD of about 0.8 and the trend up about 1pt since August, persistence alone gives about 0.65. Mean reversion from the record high and the first Union uptick in 11 weeks trim that to about 0.58. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: All three dossiers agree on the facts: the INSA series, a current median of 30.0, an inclusive threshold, about two polls a week, no market. The remaining disagreements are judgment calls about drift and mean reversion. I weighted the persistence model (about 0.65 given a ~30.1 level against a 29.75 effective cutoff) against reversion from the record high and the Union's rebound tick, landing at 0.58. The Union-uptick headline is confirmed by the Run 1 dawum/t-online report, so it is not disputed.

disagreements.verdict: Roughly balanced, with a slight edge to persistence because the level sits above the effective rounding cutoff
